# Orange Plan Academy — guided course

**Start with [the dictation order](DICTATION-ORDER.md).** The current course has 51 core teaching clips, 15 conditional Advanced clips, ten app working sessions and one device demonstration. Debt is Session 3; Allocation is Session 4.

The reviewed lessons are now in **`scripts/`**, not the former `course-v2/` workspace. [ALL-SCRIPTS.md](ALL-SCRIPTS.md) is the complete read-aloud copy. [MASTER-COURSE.md](MASTER-COURSE.md) includes production notes and checkpoints. [FILM-ORDER.md](FILM-ORDER.md) places the replaceable working-session chapters between the explanations that prepare them.

**Current status: ready for Austin's dictation and editorial approval.** This is not a claim of final recording, professional sign-off, or app-capture approval. The [remaining gates](FINALIZATION-STATUS.md) are explicit. This branch's content does not prove a merge to `main`.

[Advanced dictation](ADVANCED-DICTATION-ORDER.md) · [Member worksheets](toolkit/README.md) · [Visual/edit map](visuals/GUIDED-EDIT-MAP.md) · [Capture receipts](CAPTURE-RECEIPTS.md) · [App alignment](V1-COURSE-ALIGNMENT.md) · [Landing alignment](LANDING-PAGE-ALIGNMENT.md).

## Edit one source

Dictation edits go into the matching canonical file under `scripts/`. Read-aloud material goes only under `### Read aloud`; directions and qualifications for the editor stay in `### Production notes`. Never edit a generated teleprompter copy and assume the change reached the source.

```sh
python tools/guided_course.py build
python tools/guided_course.py check
python tools/guided_course.py test
```

These commands synchronize and check the reading copies, masters, member playback order and production lists. They do not run the financial engine, access customer accounts or deploy anything.

## Preserved sources

Original permitted dictation remains in `source-material/`. The preceding scripts, masters, tools, supporting records and full grouped guided draft are preserved under `archive/pre-guided-promotion/`. Historical files are not recording instructions. [PROMOTION-RECORD.json](PROMOTION-RECORD.json) records their hashes and the exact amendments.

Raw client calls, private financial records, secrets and font files are not included in this course promotion.
documents.FINALIZATION-STATUS.md:
# What is finished and what remains

## Finished in this editorial pass

Every one of the 51 core explanations, 15 Advanced explanations and eleven practical run sheets was read. The guided structure, example continuity, decision/checkpoint handoffs and source-derived concepts were checked. The canonical scripts, read-aloud copies, masters, dictation order and playback order now describe the same course.

The four Bitcoin paths are explained; the Reserve / Bridge / Forever visual has its reasoning restored; investment horizon is distinguished from retirement-account access. The HSA / IRA / additional workplace-plan branch is explained. The college lesson now works from parental commitment to assigned resources, gap, saving pace and affordability. Allocation now works through holdings in different accounts and an affordable post-card-payoff route. Production-only narration was removed from the relevant spoken passages. Original dictation and older scripts remain preserved.

## Austin's next work

Start dictating at 0.1 through the linked files in DICTATION-ORDER.md. The text is a complete teaching draft to react to, not a claim that the newly written lines are already Austin's words. Existing dictation is traced in DICTATION-SOURCE-MAP.md. Approve revised concepts and examples before final takes. Concept clips can use graphics added in editing; they need not be live slide presentations.

## Separate publication gates

**App recordings:** W01–W10 and product-dependent spoken claims require the actual approved build, account mode, inputs, receipt, supported controls and save/reload behavior. Starting-plan output, account composition entry, source capability receipts, transfer/import handling, return overrides, contribution routing, tax comparisons, guardrails, report/export/restore, Ask, market reports and external-AI connection/export cannot be certified by reading a design contract. Unsupported chapters remain held.

**Device demonstration:** D07 and device-specific Advanced footage require an exact manufacturer/model, firmware, backup standard, current official instructions, small test setup and independently reviewed recovery proof. No funded-primary-wallet reset as a first test. No usable secrets in footage.

**Professional content:** factual research supports the mechanisms, not a licensed opinion or member-specific execution. Tax/account access, harvesting identification, conversions, current-year healthcare interactions, lending contracts, beneficiary/trust design and insurance terms retain the targeted review named on each script. Quotes, legal documents and actual transactions need verification at use. Current sources are in PRIMARY-SOURCES.md.

**Launch offer:** this edit does not approve prices, access terms, call cadence, legal terms or a live app cutover. The supplied landing draft needs the corrections in LANDING-PAGE-ALIGNMENT.md.

No app code, hosted records, provider connections or Production settings were changed by this course work. No full-course filming-ready or launch-ready verdict is asserted.

documents.LANDING-PAGE-ALIGNMENT.md:
# Supplied landing drafts: promise and required copy updates

Reviewed the visible templates in `Orange Plan Academy Landing v1(1).html` and `Orange Plan Landing v4 - Responsive Conversion Pass(2).html`. Their illustrative numbers are not the course fixture or engine evidence. This document does not change a deployed page or approve offer terms.

The guided course now addresses the Academy's stated outputs: an honest position (Session 1); normal spending, a reserve plan and events (2); jobs and rules for debt (3); an allocation and next-dollar route (4); supported purchase records and tax questions (5); retirement funding and review rules (6); custody (7); a family handoff (8); a maintenance rhythm (9); and a plan the household can explain (10). The corresponding working sessions and toolkit provide the implementation checkpoints.

## Update before publishing the landing page

Replace the FAQ's **28 lessons / about 150 minutes / 10 captures** with: **“51 core teaching clips, a conditional Advanced library, ten app working sessions and a separate wallet-recovery demonstration. Work through one decision at a time; gathering information and completing outside actions will take additional time.”** Use measured edited runtimes later. Do not add an arbitrary shorter cap.

Replace the old curriculum counts and order: Debt is Session 3, Allocation is 4, Maintenance is 9, and reading/sharing the completed plan is 10. College is optional in Session 2; core debt, healthcare, tax and account-access explanation is no longer hidden behind an optional library.

Replace **“guardrails read as a simulation count”** with **“understand the plan's success result and use its spending-review rules.”** Full results are percent-first with the matching count below; guardrail levels and proposed spending are distinct.

Replace **“a funded reserve”** as an immediate course-completion claim with **“a reserve target, identified sources and an affordable funding plan.”** Money may take months to accumulate. Completion distinguishes decisions, saved choices and completed outside actions.

Remove the app draft's Ask example suggesting the normal user chose an 80% target. Accepted direction uses Orange Plan's normal standard, with overrides in Advanced. Do not promise all supported-source accounts are fully current or complete merely because they linked.

Keep the practical support promise, but confirm price, access length, renewal, clinics, community support, private-build scope and legal terms separately. This course edit approves none of those commercial decisions. Any specific report, AI, source connection or guardrail screenshot also waits for the actual accepted build.
documents.AUSTIN-AUTHORITY.md:
# Current course authority

Use Austin's newest explicit decisions and dictation first. Accepted app contracts govern product terminology and required behavior; actual validated captures establish what ships. The Academy promise governs the finished outcome. Slide decks govern the teaching concepts and decision sequence, with documented corrections for outdated rules. Coaching calls supply real questions and explanatory detail without becoming public client examples. Current primary verification governs changeable facts. The older master is supplemental.

The approved spine is Start Here plus ten guided sessions. Cash flow precedes debt decisions; debt claims are finalized before contribution routing. Allocation explains the current position, whole-household target, horizon, waterfall, wrapper, Traditional/Roth choice and holdings. Strategic debt is core. The example household is fictional. Healthcare contains no family medical anecdote. Custody is a trade-off and continuity decision, not a wealth ladder. Bitcoin can remain part of five-plus-year funding with explicit committed needs and fallback planning.

Keep direct explanations. Remove rhetorical “not this, but that” openings when the positive explanation works. Preserve factual distinctions and necessary warnings; do not remove a safety condition to satisfy a style scan. Define unfamiliar financial concepts, show a worked example and finish with a decision or checkpoint.

The new canonical files are complete pre-dictation drafts. Their editorial status is not Austin's voice approval, licensed sign-off, app validation or launch approval. Preserve the source files and history; never call invented connective wording prior dictation.
documents.SOURCE-MATERIAL-POLICY.md:
# Source material policy

Canonical scripts are under `scripts/`; derived copies flow outward only. Original permitted dictation under `source-material/` is immutable. Prior active material is retained in `archive/pre-guided-promotion/` and hash-checked by the build.

Raw client calls, personal financial records, medical anecdotes, account identifiers, credentials, recovery material and exact secret locations stay out of the public repository. Examples in active scripts and worksheets use the fictional Reed household or explicitly generic arithmetic. Do not upload font files.

Preserve source terminology and reasoning unless a newer owner decision, accepted product rule or documented factual correction changes it. Keep the reason in the amendment or alignment record. Historical claims about returns, providers, taxes, account limits or app behavior require current verification before they become present-tense claims. Source coverage is not proof of legal correctness or implementation.

# Primary-source verification register

Editorial verification date: 2026-09-07. Research checks mechanisms and flags current-law dependencies; it is not professional approval of the course or a student's transaction. Do not replace a current-year check with this timestamp when filming or executing later. No live market price, loan quote, school-cost quote or insurance premium is asserted.

| Area / lessons | Primary reference | Applied boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Taxable gains, records and securities; 4.7, 5.1–5.5 | IRS Publication 550 — https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550 | Basis and adjusted gain need evidence; investments and distributions differ; no assurance a rough estimate satisfies filing requirements |
| Contributions; 4.5–4.6 | IRS Publication 590-A — https://www.irs.gov/publications/p590a | Eligibility, deductions and limits differ from Roth conversions; no annual dollar limit hardcoded |
| Roth ordering, conversions and distributions; 4.6, 5.4, 6.2, A5.1, A6.3 | IRS Publication 590-B — https://www.irs.gov/publications/p590b | Regular contributions, conversions and earnings differ; qualified and conversion five-year rules differ; beneficiary rules differ from owner rules |
| Early access; 6.2, A6.3 | IRS exception chart — https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/plan-participant-employee/retirement-topics-exceptions-to-tax-on-early-distributions | Verify exact plan, qualifying separation and rollover history; governmental 457(b) is distinct |
| Workplace distribution and SEPP conditions; A6.3 | IRS 401(k) distribution rules — https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/plan-participant-employee/401k-resource-guide-plan-participants-general-distribution-rules | Rule of 55 concerns qualifying separation from that employer; SEPP duration/changes require review |
| Broker-held digital-asset identification; 5.2, A5.2 | IRS Notice 2026-20, IRB 2026-15 — https://www.irs.gov/irb/2026-15_IRB | Temporary identification relief is conditional and time-bound; a software ordering preference alone is not legal proof |
| Education choices; 2.5 | SEC 529 bulletin, January 28, 2026 — https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins/introduction-529-plans-investor-bulletin | Plan menu, qualified use, restrictions and state treatment matter; no automatic Bitcoin access |
| Education cost estimate; 2.5 | Federal Student Aid — https://studentaid.gov/articles/evaluating-financial-aid-offers/ | Compare cost of attendance less grants/scholarships; loans are financing, not a discount |
| Securities-backed borrowing; 3.5, A3.2 | FINRA — https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/securities-backed-lines-credit | Non-purpose restrictions and collateral-call risk; no permission to purchase securities with restricted proceeds |
| Home-equity contracts; 3.5, A3.2 | CFPB — https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/research-reports/issue-spotlight-home-equity-contracts-market-overview/ | Future settlement tied to home value; low/no payment is not absence of obligation |
| Plan loans; 3.5, A3.2 | IRS — https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/hardships-early-withdrawals-and-loans | Availability and repayment depend on plan; IRAs do not provide participant loans |
| Marketplace income; 6.3, A6.1 | Healthcare.gov — https://www.healthcare.gov/income-and-household-information/income/ | Coverage-year household income, relevant gains/withdrawals and changes require a consistent comparison |
| HSA changes; 4.5, 6.3, A6.1 | IRS Notice 2026-05 announcement — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/treasury-irs-provide-guidance-on-new-tax-benefits-for-health-savings-account-participants-under-the-one-big-beautiful-bill | 2026 eligibility rules changed; do not reuse a blanket old Bronze/catastrophic-plan exclusion |
| Non-insurance healthcare; 6.3, A6.1 | CrowdHealth member guide — https://www.joincrowdhealth.com/resources/member-guide | Member remains responsible; crowdfunding and insurance are different; no provider recommendation or guaranteed funding |
| Social Security timing; 6.2 | SSA — https://www.ssa.gov/benefits/retirement/planner/delayret.html | Delayed retirement credits stop at 70 for the retirement benefit; household/survivor and Medicare issues still need review |
| Safer recovery testing; 7.2, D07 | Trezor — https://trezor.io/guides/backups-recovery/general-standards/check-wallet-backup-on-model-t | Example of an official backup check before reset; not a universal procedure or hardware recommendation |
| Passphrase distinction; 7.2, A7.1 | Trezor — https://trezor.io/guides/trezor-suite/using-a-passphrase-wallet-in-trezor-suite | Passphrase derives another wallet; typo can open an empty wallet; exact backup and compatibility requirements remain |
| Account security; 7.3 | CISA — https://www.cisa.gov/audiences/small-and-medium-businesses/secure-your-business/require-multifactor-authentication | Prefer phishing-resistant options where supported; no absolute immunity claim |
| Legal-role terminology; 8.1 | California Courts — https://www.selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/probate/terms | Illustrative jurisdictional source for appointment/roles only; it does not establish law in another state |

## Review still required before publication or individual use

Verify the actual year's tax, credits, required distributions, deductions, wash-sale/identification rules, benefit eligibility and account facts. IRS documents do not authorize a recommended allocation, tax-basis reconstruction method or exact conversion amount. State residency, trusts, fiduciary duties, beneficiary documents and insurance coverage require appropriate jurisdictional/contract review. Wallet configuration and device-specific recovery need current official documentation and an independent test of the exact setup.

The course deliberately avoids unsupported universal tax-free borrowing, automatic positive spreads, guaranteed Bitcoin recovery, no-risk custody or no-forced-sale claims. The numerical examples are arithmetic illustrations, independently checked in ARITHMETIC-CHECKS.json; they are not calibrated financial-model results.

Use one monthly convention. Income before which costs? ____  Spending includes what? ____  Reference period/method: ____

The separate $387.50 employer match goes to retirement; it is not another spendable $387.50. The $4,000 provision is a teaching assumption, not a tax calculation.

Reed check: $7,200 × 6 = $43,200 target; $32,000 assigned; $11,200 gap. $500 monthly would fill it in 22.4 months before interest or withdrawals: 22 full deposits and a final $200 in month 23. Compare that pace with the risks; choosing a target does not fill it.

documents.toolkit/03-life-events-college.md:
# Life events and college commitment

For each expected change write: what happens; when; amount; today's/future dollars; one-time/recurring; income/expense/debt/property effects; source of funding; certainty; and what will change when the event becomes actual. A possibility stays a scenario. Count a home down payment, mortgage, ongoing costs and property value in their separate roles.

## College

Parental commitment per child: ____  What is included: ____  Start year / payment years: ____  Cost source / aid assumptions: ____

Use school cost-of-attendance and net-price estimates. Grants/scholarships reduce the amount to fund; loans create repayment obligations. Check the actual borrower's current limits, terms and repayment capacity before depending on a loan.

Worked benchmark: $20,000 × four years = $80,000 commitment. For illustration, $29,000 of the household's $58,000 education resources is assigned to the older child; the other $29,000 remains for the younger child. Confirm actual beneficiaries before moving money. Gap: $80,000 − $29,000 = $51,000. Prefunding that gap over 60 months at flat costs and zero growth is $850/month.

This is a first comparison, not a complete education projection. Add cost inflation, payment dates, investment outcomes, taxable sales, future cash flow and overlap between children. A later saving start needs a new monthly calculation. During the Reed card-payoff phase there is no unassigned $850: the household must change a claim, source, commitment or timing.

| Funding source | Amount / years | Already assigned elsewhere? | Reliability / tax or account condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing education account | | | |
| New saving | | | |
| Future household cash flow | | | |
| Taxable investments / Bitcoin | | | |
| Student earnings / confirmed aid | | | |
| Student or parent borrowing | | | |

Bitcoin can remain a source around five-plus years when the household accepts the risk and has a credible fallback. Identify the committed near-term payments that need dependable funding. The one-third idea is an optional source-mix discussion, not an affordability rule.

documents.toolkit/04-debt-financing.md:
# Debt jobs and financing comparison

Inventory each debt: balance, required payment, APR, fixed/variable status, term/reset/maturity, collateral, guarantees, repayment source and source document date. Unused credit is access, not an owned asset.

Your monthly lens: required payments ÷ gross monthly income. Your balance-sheet lens: total debt ÷ included gross assets. State what is excluded. Stress assets and income separately; a ratio alone does not prove payments are affordable.

Reed included assets $1,996,000; debt $444,500; scoped net worth $1,551,500; debt/assets about 22.27%. Vehicle and equipment/business values are omitted while their debts remain. The deliberately partial stress leaves $1,217,200 of included assets and about 36.52% debt/assets. This is not a full worst case.

Give each debt one job, a reason for keep/pay-extra/refinance/pay-off/review, and a trigger. The adopted Reed plan gives the card $1,200 extra; the final claim must return to the cash-flow bridge.

## Compare the same purchase

| Alternative | Cash now | Monthly cost | Total cost / exit balance | Collateral or guarantee | Failure / fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cash | | | | | |

Read use restrictions, rate resets, balloon payments, fees and remedies. A cash-out refinance reprices the replacement balance. A home-equity contract can owe a substantial later settlement. A non-purpose securities line restricts investment use. An unsupported contract needs a separate reviewed schedule, not a fake amortizing substitute.

## Operating rules before borrowing

Purpose: ____  Credible repayment: ____  Maximum payment and total exposure: ____  Personal review level: ____  Contractual action level: ____  Cash/collateral response resources: ____  Maturity/refinancing fallback: ____  No-go conditions: ____  Monitor / backup operator: ____

LTV = full debt ÷ collateral value. With fixed debt and an illustrative 80% liquidation threshold, 50% initial LTV reaches it after a 37.5% collateral-price fall; 25% initial reaches it after 68.75%. Accrued interest, fees, changing terms, access and counterparty failure can worsen the result. These are not safe levels or lender terms.

# Four views and the next-dollar plan

Review in order: current accounts/holdings → household target → timeframe needs → one contribution pool → usable account → Traditional/Roth choice → specific investment → outside actions.

## Current holdings by account

| Reed teaching account | Bitcoin exposure | Stocks | Cash / short-term Treasury category | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Checking | 0 | 0 | 18,000 | 18,000 |
| Reserve savings | 0 | 0 | 32,000 | 32,000 |
| Taxable brokerage | 0 | 90,000 | 25,000 | 115,000 |
| Direct Bitcoin | 340,000 | 0 | 0 | 340,000 |
| Professional Bitcoin custody | 70,000 | 0 | 0 | 70,000 |
| Alex Traditional 401(k) | 123,000 | 287,000 | 0 | 410,000 |
| Morgan Solo 401(k) | 38,000 | 57,000 | 0 | 95,000 |
| Alex Roth IRA | 116,000 | 29,000 | 0 | 145,000 |
| Morgan Traditional IRA | 41,000 | 41,000 | 0 | 82,000 |
| Total | 728,000 | 504,000 | 75,000 | 1,307,000 |

The fixed $100,000/BTC price is invented. Home, HSA and 529 are excluded from this general allocation denominator, not erased from net worth. Treasury exposure is a teaching grouping; identify the real security and its actual classification in the app. Spot Bitcoin funds stay securities, not native Bitcoin for custody or transfers.

Hypothetical 60/34/6 target: $784,200 Bitcoin, $444,380 stocks, $78,420 cash category. The Bitcoin difference is $56,200, not an instruction to trade. A 70% Bitcoin-only decline reduces this portfolio by $509,600 before other changes. Test both the dollars and a prolonged weak period.

## Timeframe and wrapper

Reserve: near-term dependable funds. Bridge: approaching spending with its own flexibility. Forever: later money with time to remain invested. The original 0–3 / 4–10 / 10+ year picture is an illustration. Now / before59½ / after59½ concerns access and must be evaluated separately.

For each receiving dollar, record job/date, account/owner, permitted access, available investments, tax treatment, costs and intended holding. HSA / IRA / additional workplace saving is a comparison after the match; taxable early-access needs, menu or costs can change the order.

Traditional/Roth comparison uses equal pretax resources. At an illustrative 20% tax rate, $1,000 pretax in Traditional doubles to $2,000 and leaves $1,600 after that tax. $800 after-tax in Roth doubles to $1,600 on a qualified withdrawal. Future tax rates, eligibility, limits, access and the use of today's deduction change the comparison.

## Current and future routing

Current adopted pool: $2,475 = $775 employee + $500 reserve + $1,200 extra card; residual zero. Employer match $387.50 is separate. After card payoff, $405 required payment + $1,200 extra releases $1,605, subject to an actual updated cash-flow check.

Illustrative future comparison: $1,000 personally held Bitcoin + $605 taxable stock fund = $1,605. The reserve build continues. This is neither current available money nor an engine recommendation. Reassess when the reserve fills rather than silently adding another $500.

# Tax decision and professional handoff

Start with a specific question: a proposed sale, a conversion, a distribution or a current-year payment gap. Keep liability separate from how it is paid.

For a purchase record, preserve quantity, date, amount paid, fees as supported, account/wallet, transfers and remaining units. Unknown is unknown. Collect actual statements/exports and evidence before discussing a reconstruction with the tax professional; the course does not certify a guessed price window.

At the invented $100,000 sale price, selling 0.2 BTC produces $20,000 before fees. Basis from the $58,000-per-BTC lot is $11,600 and gain $8,400; from the $16,000 lot basis $3,200 and gain $16,800; from the $52,000 lot basis $10,400 and gain $9,600. Verify actual unit identification and holding period before execution. A software HIFO setting alone is not filing evidence.

Map working income, lower-income years, Social Security, required distributions and possible state changes. Compare conversion with intentional Traditional spending and no change. Include current tax funding, opportunity cost, future taxes, healthcare interactions, early-access liquidity and total after-tax outcome.

Proposed action: ____  Current-year income and uncertainty: ____  Account/units: ____  Supported basis: ____  Tax funding source: ____  Current versus future effect: ____  Question for CPA: ____  Deadline: ____

After professional verification and outside execution, record the actual transaction and reconcile it. Keep planned and completed conversions separate. FORM 8949 TAX DATA is a handoff export; the filed return and carryforwards still require review and continuity.

# Maintain and explain the plan

Monthly date: ____  Annual review month: ____  Separate tax, maturity or collateral deadlines: ____

A quiet monthly pass checks changed accounts/activity, income/spending, expected events and the saved result's as-of state. Resolve one meaningful issue at a time. Record zero to three actions; zero is valid when nothing needs attention. Source-proven automatic updates do not require re-entering the same activity.

Annual review covers spending/reserve, allocation, all relevant debts and LTV, taxes, custody and family/estate arrangements. Update facts first. Compare strategy changes separately. Save the supported readable report and appropriate data backup; verify restoration rather than treating file creation as proof.

Where we stand: ____
What we save and why: ____
When the plan supports work becoming optional, under which assumptions: ____
How early and later retirement years are funded: ____
What could force a change, sale or loan response: ____
Who starts the family process if the usual operator is unavailable: ____
Our next one to three actions and review dates: ____

documents.COURSE-ARCHITECTURE-V2.md:
# Guided Academy architecture

The canonical teaching sequence is Start Here, then ten guided plan-building sessions: First working plan; Cash flow, reserve and life events; Debt and leverage; Allocation and the next dollar; Tax strategy; Retirement paycheck; Custody; Family handoff; Maintenance; Read and share your plan.

Each session teaches the decision, explains the mechanism, works through the fictional Reed household, and gives the member a completion check. The associated app chapters put the decisions into the correct place. Build & improve guides implementation; it is not a second editor or a fixed promise about the order of tasks the application will show.

Debt precedes final allocation because extra debt payments change the cash available to invest. Allocation then moves from the current portfolio through the whole-household target, timeframe needs, contribution waterfall, account eligibility, Traditional versus Roth, holdings inside each account, and the outside execution list.

Core teaching contains 51 clips, including optional college planning. The conditional Advanced library contains 15 clips. Ten app working sessions and one external device demonstration are captured separately. Exact playback chapter placement is in FILM-ORDER.md; script identities and hashes are in COURSE-MANIFEST.json.

The worksheets support decisions and record follow-through. They do not substitute for app-generated projections, legal documents, professional tax review, actual insurance quotes, provider contracts or tested recovery. A fictional arithmetic example is labeled as such.

Talking-head narration and graphics added in editing are supported. The existing decks provide conceptual visual references; visuals/GUIDED-EDIT-MAP.md is an edit brief, not a completed graphics package. Product-dependent footage remains held until matching capture receipts prove the released behavior.

All new wording is an Austin-review draft. Current dictation and owner decisions govern tone and planning judgment; accepted app contracts govern intended behavior; verified released behavior governs filmed claims. See AUSTIN-AUTHORITY.md and FINALIZATION-STATUS.md.

W01: This is where we will build the first version of the plan. Start with the next task and follow it to the record we need to complete.
I am adding what this household actually owns. The account tells us the owner and tax treatment; the investments explain what the money is holding.
Read what this source supplied. A current balance, a list of investments and purchase details answer different questions.
We know the account total. Now we need to identify the investments behind it. Entering what is held today is separate from entering an actual purchase.
This history belongs to an existing position. Check that adding the evidence has not counted the same Bitcoin twice.
Follow the money from income through taxes, living costs and required payments. The employee contribution uses household money; the employer contribution is additional retirement money.
Fifty-two is the date Alex would like to make work optional. We will compare the plan with that preference after the real inputs are in place.
Here are the growth and inflation assumptions. Change one in the comparison so we can see what it affects.
Read the result and its date together. The percentage and the simulation count describe the same run; check the horizon and what information it used.
Now ask about something in the completed picture. Trace the explanation back to the actual number before deciding what to change.
W02: This is the amount available before the employee contribution. Subtract that once, then decide what the remaining dollars can do.
We are checking the spending the plan should carry forward. A transfer between our accounts does not add another household expense.
The spending change is a proposal until the household makes it. Here is the outside action that makes the saving real.
The reserve target comes from the essential monthly amount and the number of months. Next identify which existing dollars genuinely count toward it.
We have a reserve pace. The next session sets the extra-debt claim, and Allocation will finish the investment route from what remains.
This is an expected change, with an amount and a date. A possibility stays in the scenario comparison until the household adopts it.
Begin with the parent commitment. Assign the education resources once, calculate the gap, and check whether the proposed saving fits the same cash flow.
W03: For each debt, confirm what is owed, the required payment and the terms that can change. The available credit line is not another asset.
These ratios answer different questions. One shows monthly payment pressure; the other shows debt against the assets included in this balance sheet.
The extra card payment uses twelve hundred dollars from the adopted cash-flow plan. Read the actual payoff calculation before writing down a date.
Keep the same project and date across the alternatives. Compare cash now, payments, total obligations and what is pledged.
Before using leverage, write down the repayment source, review trigger and response. A market rebound is uncertain, so include a fallback.
Return to cash flow and check that the debt decision appears once. The reserve, employee contribution and extra payment must fit the same pool.
W04: Read this portfolio by investment, timing, account and actual holding. Confirm which assets are included before comparing percentages.
This target is a choice we are testing. Translate the drawdown into dollars and check what the household would need to do.
Now identify which money funds the early years and which remains for later. Account access and investment horizon are separate questions.
This phase uses all the available money. A contribution that starts after the card is paid off needs a later date and a new cash-flow check.
Choose a usable account with the investment menu, tax treatment and access the dollar needs.
Compare Traditional and Roth using the same pretax resources, then check the effect on household cash flow.
Choose what each contribution buys. Different account mixes can add up to the same household target.
Here is what the plan saves, and here is what the household still needs to change with payroll, the broker or another provider.
W05: The sale proceeds are the same. The basis of the units identified for sale changes the gain; the actual identification process still needs verification.
Add the available activity to the existing account. Read duplicates and missing details without increasing a balance already counted.
The roadmap shows when taxable income may change. Withholding is how tax is paid, not the tax liability itself.
Include the cash used to pay conversion tax and the future after-tax outcome. Compare with leaving the plan unchanged.
This is a possible transaction. Verification, outside execution and recording the actual result happen as separate steps.
This export is tax data for the professional. Check its coverage and reconcile it with the completed return.
W06: Start with the annual cash need. Include the taxes, required payments and events as well as living costs, then identify the income already arriving.
Check the access and benefit dates for each spouse. Every early year needs an account that can actually provide the money.
Use a realistic healthcare cost and transition date. Compare its income effects alongside the tax decision.
Choose the account withdrawal mix, then the investments sold within it. Read the effect on this year and later years.
The reserve gives the plan time in a difficult market. Check what happens when cash approaches its floor and what funds the next refill.
Read the borrowing benefit beside the additional risk. Follow interest, debt, collateral and repayment through the difficult years.
Compare the same starting plan with one focused change. Check which assumptions were changed and which were inherited.
The guardrail status opens a spending decision. Read the proposed amount, its limits and the funding effect before saving.
W07: Name the job and the control preference for each meaningful pool. Then record the protection gained and the risk still retained.
Record what the recovery test actually proved. A pending test stays pending.
Choose the largest shared failure to address first. Security changes happen with the provider or device; the plan records the result.
The family needs the safe starting point and the next action. Recovery secrets stay out of this record.
D07: This is a separate small test setup. Confirm the device and the current official procedure before beginning.
Secret-generation and backup material remain off camera and outside the recorded files.
The PIN, backup and any passphrase have different jobs. Keep the correct recovery material offline.
Check the receiving destination through the trusted device process before the small test transfer.
Check the backup before any reset. Use the supported method for this device and backup standard.
Restore only within the reviewed test procedure and confirm the intended wallet, with secrets absent from the footage.
Verify a small outgoing transaction and its fee through the same trusted process.
Record the successful test and what remains untested. A more complex setup needs its own complete recovery proof.
W08: Identify who starts the process, the backup person and the legal documents that give the appropriate authority.
Connect the legal role to the actual recovery or institution process. Keep unanswered legal and technical questions explicit.
The letter starts with one verified contact and clear warnings. Test whether the recipient knows the first step.
A communication backstop needs a harmless delivery test. It delivers direction, never signing keys.
Record the risk the household retains or transfers and the policy question requiring licensed review.
W09: On a quiet month, check what actually changed and stop when the relevant facts are current.
Resolve the specific exception. A snoozed question is still open; a correction should explain what changed.
Walk the six review areas using the current facts. Tax and collateral deadlines have their own timing.
Update the real income change, then compare a strategy separately. Read when the saved result has caught up.
Write down the decisions, outside actions and review dates. Keep the supported report and a tested data-recovery process.
W10: Read the position, direction, risks and next actions. Check that each number matches the source record and saved result.
Look at the years where funding changes: retirement, a benefit beginning, a large event and later taxable distributions.
Explain the plan in ordinary language. Ask your listener to repeat the funding path and the first family-response action.
Prepare the exact questions and relevant evidence for each professional. A prepared packet is separate from advice received.
Save the dated plan and action list. This becomes the starting point for the next annual comparison.
